correctness.rationale: For each fixed n>=2, exact cancellation from h_j(n)-h_j(n-1)=1/[nP_(j-1)(n)] yields Q_j(n)=P_j(n)/P_j(n-1)=1+(1/n)sum_(i=1)^j 1/P_i(n-1). At n=2, h_j(2)=(j+2)/(j+1) and P_j(2)=(j+2)/2. Induct on fixed endpoint n: if P_j(n-1)~j/(n-1)*product_(r=1)^(n-3)log_r j, the reciprocal sum is asymptotic to (n-1)log_(n-2)j by the divergent iterated-logarithm integral and tail squeeze; multiplying Q_j(n) by P_j(n-1) yields j/n product_(r=1)^(n-2)log_r j. The k=2 term in h_j(n)-1 is exactly 1/(j+1); k=3 gives 1/(j log j), all finitely many k>=4 terms are little-o at fixed n. These establish both stated limits, not uniform in growing n. Independently reconstructed exact rational h,P,Q and recurrence for j<=12,n<=7; finite tests do not prove asymptotics.
